text:
Deaf little song, sad,
discordant song;
song trilled sotto voce
and stolen from labor,
behind the mistress's back;
at the master's patience;
deaf little song, sad,
slave song, song,
song of a young slave girl who feels
memory is treacherous;
song of filing chains
beneath its murmur;
song of outpourings
drowned in fear;
song of a slave that tastes
of forbidden fruit:
—you appear to me wholly
in two eyes and a voice.


Between her teeth, barely heard,
words of rebellion:
“War on another's fortune,
war on another's pain!
Sweep their house, wind,
for I will not sweep it.
Spin them the fleece, spider,
for I will not spin it.
San Telmo, light the sails,
San Pascual, tend the hearth.
Today the needle pricked me
and the spindle broke;
and such is the tyranny
of this dissimulation,
that though rare longings
swell my heart,
I have looks of defiance
and a voice of resignation.”


Fierce were her eyes,
and hoarse and mild her voice;
refined imaginings
and a plebeian heart.
Her mother, being simple,
did not know how to marry her, no.
A witness to other lives,
her spirit betrays her.
Deaf little song, sad,
slave song, song:
—you appear to me wholly
in two eyes and a voice.

translation.title: The Tune of the Enemy Servant
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the servant’s covert song, named saints, household labor, and the tension between rebellious eyes and a resigned voice.
